core_obligations: Choose a surjection R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A and elements y_1, ..., y_m of B generating B over A (proof lines 20989-20990).
Use finiteness of A -> B to find monic polynomials P_j(T) in R[x_1, ..., x_n][T] with P_j(y_j) = 0 in B (proof lines 20991-20993).
Exhibit the commutative square from R[x_1, ..., x_n] to R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_m]/(P_j(y_j)) over A -> B (proof lines 20994-21001).

Use that the top arrow is a finite and finitely presented ring map, together with the Algebra statement on finite finitely presented extensions and the definition of relative finite presentation, to conclude (proof lines 21002-21005).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a finite map A -> B of finite type R-algebras, and a B-module M, and asserts that M is an A-module finitely presented relative to R if and only if it is a B-module finitely presented relative to R (source lines 20979-20986). The proof is a presentation argument. It chooses a surjection R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A and elements y_1, ..., y_m of B generating B over A (proof lines 20989-20990). Since A -> B is finite, each y_i satisfies a monic equation with coefficients in A, so there are monic polynomials P_j(T) in R[x_1, ..., x_n][T] with P_j(y_j) = 0 in B (proof lines 20991-20993). The proof then exhibits the commutative square from R[x_1, ..., x_n] to R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_m]/(P_j(y_j)) over A -> B (proof lines 20994-21001). Since the top arrow is a finite and finitely presented ring map, the conclusion follows from the Algebra statement on finite finitely presented extensions together with the definition of relative finite presentation (proof lines 21002-21005). The non-routine content is the construction of a presentation of B over a polynomial ring by killing monic equations, which is what makes the top arrow finitely presented as well as finite.
